findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…'), against the hero's 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: The pull quote uses the button's shape: an edged panel with dovetail handles on both sides. That shape is the only thing marking 'Write to Mark' as the page's one action. So the same look means 'press me' in the hero and 'read me' in the article. On article pages, where the quote will appear most, the handles stop meaning 'act'.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor who reads an article and then looks for how to contact Mark. They have already seen the handled panel as a quote that does nothing, so a handled panel no longer stands out as the thing to press. Angélique will also be adding quotes to posts, so the shape will appear more and more often as decoration.

findings.where: Palette rule 'minium: headings, the one action', as rendered in the hero name and role, the article title and the motion sketch's 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED'
findings.fault: The colour meant for the action is also used on every heading, so it doesn't belong to the action. In the first screen the largest minium mass is the two-line name and role, not the button. Anyone scanning by colour for the one action lands on a heading first. The candidate's own direction says the one accent 'flows to the action', but it doesn't.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor deciding whether and how to get in touch. The red that should lead the eye to 'Write to Mark' is spent on text that can't be acted on, both on the homepage and on article pages, where minium headings sit alone with no action near them.

findings.where: Hero, 'Write to Mark' (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com), and the nav's 'Contact'
findings.fault: The page's only contact action is a mailto link, and Mark's address isn't written anywhere on the page. If the visitor has no desktop mail client set up, the button does nothing or opens an unconfigured app. They are then left without a way to reach Mark, since they can't see an address to copy.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank and agency staff working in browser webmail or on locked-down machines. For them a mailto opens nothing useful, and the site's one job, getting them in touch with Mark, fails silently.

findings.where: Motion sketch, 'Lay again' (a button that replays the animation)
findings.fault: An in-page action is styled as an underlined text link. The page reserves underlining for links, as on the article's 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' link just beside it. The same underline therefore means both 'go somewhere' and 'replay here'.
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder reviewing the tile. They may expect 'Lay again' to open a page or a file, as the underlined lecture link does, rather than replay the arches in place.
